cards.title: World Notes: The Real Flat Stanley Project
cards.sub: A real thing behind one of our books
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: In 1995, a 3rd grade teacher in Canada named Dale Hubert had an idea. His class read Flat Stanley. Then each student colored a paper Stanley and mailed him to a friend or family member far away.
The person who got the paper Stanley took a picture with him and wrote back about his adventures.
Today, kids all over the world still mail paper Stanleys, just like Stanley traveled in an envelope in the book.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. This is our last week together. You pick one character and show the good character inside them.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first: word parts from the year, three big words, and one last editing job.
transcripts.guide2: Read about the 7 pillars. Then choose your character.
transcripts.guide3: Today you plan: your character and two pillars.

notes.wordParts: Word parts I know: -y and -ness mean being something, -ous means full of, -ful means full of, -less means without, un- means not, re- means again.
notes.grammar: Editing checklist: capitals on names and the first word, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, a comma before and/but/so when it joins two complete thoughts, and the right past form, like went.
notes.spelling: Find the base word first. Then check what was added: drop the silent e (hope, hoping), double the last letter (hop, hopping), change y to i (cry, cried), or add -es (box, boxes).
notes.wgrd: The 7 pillars of good character are honesty, respect, courtesy, responsibility, courage, service and perseverance. Our books show all of them.
vocab: doing the right thing even when no one is watching
understanding and sharing the feelings of another person
the ability to keep going after something hard

items.t: Lucy keeps saying Narnia is real, even when the others think she is making it up. (The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe)
items.why: Honesty: she tells the truth even when it is hard.

items.t: Edmund tells Peter and Susan that he and Lucy were only pretending about Narnia. (The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe)
items.why: That was a lie, so it is not honesty. Edmund changes later in the book.

items.t: Stanley stays in a picture frame all night to help catch the sneak thieves. (Flat Stanley)
items.why: Service: he helps the museum and asks for nothing back.
